BOZEMAN, Mont., October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Global analytics software leader FICO (NYSE: FICO) announced today that United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM), the nation's number one mortgage lender, is reaffirming its commitment to utilizing FICO Scores on all credit pulls across its broker lending operations, to help ensure borrowers receive the most favorable pricing and financing opportunities available.

By helping lenders understand risk more accurately, FICO Scores support more precise mortgage pricing, helping borrowers secure competitive loan terms based on their individual credit profile while supporting the safety and soundness of the housing finance system.
"Our work with UWM is driven by our shared commitment to helping more consumers achieve the dream of homeownership," said Julie May, vice president and general manager of B2B FICO Scores. Company: FICO
Jan research (many sources; citations and numbers checked by code against each source):
- UWM reaffirms commitment to FICO Scores on all credit pulls for broker lending operations [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- Wells Fargo maintains Buy rating on FICO with $800 price target [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/FICO/pressreleases/4978946/wells-fargo-sticks-to-their-buy-rating-for-fair-isaac-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- Fair Isaac Corporation: Deutsche Bank reduces target price from USD 1,658 to USD 744 [https://www.marketscreener.com/news/analyst-recommendations-nike-amd-fair-isaac-intel-rambusa--ce785dd8d180f421] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- UWM reaffirms commitment to using FICO Scores on all credit pulls across its broker lending operations to help borrowers receive favorable pricing and financing opportunities. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO Scores are used by 90% of top U.S. lenders for consistent, fair, and informed credit decisions. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO Score 10T is the most predictive credit score for mortgage lending and outperforms alternative models across all major loan categories. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO Score 10T Free Access Program allows participating lenders to receive FICO Score 10T alongside Classic FICO Score through dual processing at no additional fee. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO Score 10T adoption by mortgage lenders has surpassed 70% [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 1 in 4 borrowers are seeing better outcomes with VantageScore 4.0, which is expected to become 2 in 5 soon. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO Score 10T will be available for FHA mortgage underwriting starting January 1, 2027. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- FICO holds more than 200 US and foreign patents on technologies that increase profitability, customer satisfaction and growth for businesses. [https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/uwm-reaffirms-commitment-fico-scores-202000308.html] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- Wells Fargo maintains a Buy rating on FICO with a price target of $800.00 [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/FICO/pressreleases/4978946/wells-fargo-sticks-to-their-buy-rating-for-fair-isaac-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 52% of EMEA institutions report increasing fraud complexity as their top fraud prevention challenge, up from 40% globally. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 48% of EMEA respondents cite effective AI integration as a top challenge for fraud prevention. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 36% of EMEA institutions report fraud attempts rising by more than 25% over the past 24 months. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 28% of EMEA institutions report financial losses from fraud growing more than 25% over the past two years. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 86% of EMEA institutions see a unified, enterprise-wide fraud strategy as essential, with 38% prioritizing it as critical. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 51% of EMEA institutions report false positive rates above 15%, causing customer friction. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- 46% of EMEA fraud decisions are influenced by third-party vendor models, compared to 24% from in-house models. [https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/ai-arms-race-reshaping-fraud-threat-emea-fico/] (2026-10-06; NEW)
- Fair Isaac stock traded at EUR 595.25 on October 5, 2026, up 1.19 percent from the prior close of EUR 588.25. [https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/baird-cuts-fair-isaac-target-to-usd-1-070-for-fair-isaac-stock/70232913] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- Wells Fargo lowers FICO price target from $950 to $800, maintaining Overweight rating [https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FICO/price-targets] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- FICO research shows 52% of EMEA financial institutions cite increasing fraud complexity as their top fraud prevention challenge, up from 40% globally. [https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-arms-race-radically-reshaping-080000081.html] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- 48% of EMEA respondents rank effective AI integration as a top challenge for fraud prevention. [https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-arms-race-radically-reshaping-080000081.html] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- FICO's Enterprise Fraud Solution uses AI and ML models trained on billions of tagged transactions from over 10,000 financial institutions. [https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-arms-race-radically-reshaping-080000081.html] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- 86% of EMEA institutions see a unified, enterprise-wide fraud strategy as essential for fraud prevention. [https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-arms-race-radically-reshaping-080000081.html] (2026-10-05; NEW)
- 51% of EMEA institutions report false positive rates above 15% in fraud controls. [https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-arms-race-radically-reshaping-080000081.html] (2026-10-05; NEW)

Consumer Discretionary - Wireless, Cable and Satellite Stocks Q2 In Review: Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) Vs Peers
The end of the earnings season is always a good time to take a step back and see who shined (and who didn't). Let's take a look at how consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks fared in Q2, starting with Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR).
The Consumer Discretionary sector, by definition, is made up of companies selling non-essential goods and services. When economic conditions deteriorate or tastes shift, consumers can easily cut back or eliminate these purchases. For long-term investors with five-year holding periods, this creates a structural challenge: the sector is inherently hit-driven, with low switching costs and fickle customers. As a result, only a handful of companies can reliably grow demand and compound earnings over long periods, which is why our bar is high and High Quality ratings are rare.Wireless, cable, and satellite companies provide pay-TV, broadband internet, and mobile connectivity through large fixed-infrastructure networks. Tailwinds include growing bandwidth consumption, bundling opportunities across video, internet, and wireless services, and rural broadband subsidies from government programs. However, headwinds are pronounced: cord-cutting continues to erode traditional video subscriber bases, capital expenditure requirements for network upgrades (such as fiber overbuilds and 5G rollouts) are substantial, and aggressive promotional pricing among competitors compresses margins. Regulatory oversight on pricing and net neutrality adds uncertainty, while streaming platforms increasingly bypass traditional distributors, reducing the value of the legacy pay-TV bundle.
The 7 consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks we track reported a mixed Q2. As a group, revenues were in line with analysts' consensus estimates.
Amidst this news, share prices of the companies have had a rough stretch. On average, they are down 12% since the latest earnings results.
Operating as Spectrum, Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) is a leading telecommunications company offering cable television, high-speed internet, and voice services across the United States.
Charter reported revenues of $13.53 billion, down 1.7% year on year. This print was in line with analysts' expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with a beat of analysts' EPS estimates but a miss of analysts' EBITDA estimates.
"We operate in a competitive environment across all of our products, and our strategy for growing connectivity services is simple -- deliver the best products, at the best overall value, with the best service," said Chris Winfrey, President and CEO of Charter.
The market seems disappointed with the results as the stock is down 13.5% since reporting and currently trades at $109.39.

Formerly known as American Cable Systems, Comcast (NASDAQ:CMCSA) is a multinational telecommunications company offering a wide range of services.
Comcast reported revenues of $29.57 billion, up 4.7% year on year, outperforming analysts' expectations by 1%. The business had a satisfactory quarter with a beat of analysts' EPS estimates.
Comcast delivered the biggest analyst estimate beat and fastest revenue growth in the group. Although it had a fine quarter compared to its peers, the market seems unhappy with the results as the stock is down 8.2% since reporting. It currently trades at $21.59.
Is now the time to buy Comcast? Access our full analysis of the earnings results here, it's free.
Founded in 1986, Cable One (NYSE:CABO) provides high-speed internet, cable television, and telephone services, primarily in smaller markets across the United States.
Cable One reported revenues of $348.9 million, down 8.4% year on year, in line with analysts' expectations. It was a slower quarter as it posted a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and a miss of analysts' EBITDA estimates.
Cable One delivered the slowest revenue growth among its peers. As expected, the stock is down 72.6% since the results and currently trades at $12.18.
Read our full analysis of Cable One's results here.
Founded by Alexander Graham Bell, AT&T (NYSE:T) is a multinational telecomm conglomerate providing a range of communications and internet services.
AT&T reported revenues of $31.56 billion, up 2.3% year on year. This number missed analysts' expectations by 0.6%. Zooming out, it was actually a satisfactory quarter as it recorded a beat of analysts' EPS estimates.
The stock is up 9.3% since reporting and currently trades at $24.34.

Optimum Communications reported revenues of $2.02 billion, down 5.8% year on year. This result lagged analysts' expectations by 0.5%. It was a slower quarter as it also recorded a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and EBITDA in line with analysts' estimates.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. could pose a growing threat to terrestrial broadband providers, particularly in rural and lower-density markets, MoffettNathanson analyst Craig Moffett said Tuesday as Starlink begins deploying higher-capacity V3 satellites.
Starlink Poses Bigger Threat to Comcast and Charter
The analyst sees SpaceX's Starlink becoming a more credible competitor to terrestrial broadband as Starship enables higher-capacity satellite deployments, although he expects fiber and cable networks to retain important speed advantages.
Moffett told CNBC that Starlink presents a much greater competitive challenge to terrestrial broadband providers such as Comcast Corp. and Charter Communications Inc. than to traditional wireless carriers such as AT&T Inc. and Verizon Communications Inc..

"The terrestrial broadband business where they deliver ISP service is a very credible product and will have a direct impact. It already is having a significant impact," Moffett said.
Investors are now trying to determine whether Starlink's impact will remain concentrated in rural and low-density markets or expand further into suburban and potentially some urban areas.
Moffett said the technology remains best suited to rural markets but can also serve some customers in denser areas.
V3 Satellites Strengthen Starlink's Offering
SpaceX's first Starship orbital flight marked an important milestone because the rocket deployed 26 V3 Starlink satellites, which Moffett said carry substantially more capacity and should improve the service.
However, he expects the transition to take time. Moffett said it will be after 2030 before most of the Starlink constellation consists of V3 satellites.

Even with V3 satellites, he does not expect Starlink to match the speeds offered by terrestrial fiber or cable broadband.
That leaves pricing and customer segmentation as major competitive factors. Starlink could compete more effectively for value-oriented customers who prioritize lower costs over maximum broadband performance.
Moffett compared Starlink's challenge with the pressure Comcast and Charter already face from fixed wireless access.
The cable operators have responded by bundling broadband with wireless services, a strategy Moffett said has proven relatively successful.
The key question is how far Starlink can expand beyond its natural strength in rural markets and take customers from traditional broadband providers without matching the speed and quality of fiber and cable networks.

Consumer Discretionary - Wireless, Cable and Satellite Stocks Q2 In Review: Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) Vs Peers
The end of the earnings season is always a good time to take a step back and see who shined (and who didn't). Let's take a look at how consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks fared in Q2, starting with Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR).
The Consumer Discretionary sector, by definition, is made up of companies selling non-essential goods and services. When economic conditions deteriorate or tastes shift, consumers can easily cut back or eliminate these purchases. For long-term investors with five-year holding periods, this creates a structural challenge: the sector is inherently hit-driven, with low switching costs and fickle customers. As a result, only a handful of companies can reliably grow demand and compound earnings over long periods, which is why our bar is high and High Quality ratings are rare.Wireless, cable, and satellite companies provide pay-TV, broadband internet, and mobile connectivity through large fixed-infrastructure networks. Tailwinds include growing bandwidth consumption, bundling opportunities across video, internet, and wireless services, and rural broadband subsidies from government programs. However, headwinds are pronounced: cord-cutting continues to erode traditional video subscriber bases, capital expenditure requirements for network upgrades (such as fiber overbuilds and 5G rollouts) are substantial, and aggressive promotional pricing among competitors compresses margins. Regulatory oversight on pricing and net neutrality adds uncertainty, while streaming platforms increasingly bypass traditional distributors, reducing the value of the legacy pay-TV bundle.
The 7 consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks we track reported a mixed Q2. As a group, revenues were in line with analysts' consensus estimates.
Amidst this news, share prices of the companies have had a rough stretch. On average, they are down 12% since the latest earnings results.
Operating as Spectrum, Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) is a leading telecommunications company offering cable television, high-speed internet, and voice services across the United States.
Charter reported revenues of $13.53 billion, down 1.7% year on year. This print was in line with analysts' expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with a beat of analysts' EPS estimates but a miss of analysts' EBITDA estimates.
"We operate in a competitive environment across all of our products, and our strategy for growing connectivity services is simple -- deliver the best products, at the best overall value, with the best service," said Chris Winfrey, President and CEO of Charter.
The market seems disappointed with the results as the stock is down 13.5% since reporting and currently trades at $109.39.

Comcast delivered the biggest analyst estimate beat and fastest revenue growth in the group. Although it had a fine quarter compared to its peers, the market seems unhappy with the results as the stock is down 8.2% since reporting. It currently trades at $21.59.

Cable One reported revenues of $348.9 million, down 8.4% year on year, in line with analysts' expectations. It was a slower quarter as it posted a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and a miss of analysts' EBITDA estimates.
Cable One delivered the slowest revenue growth among its peers. As expected, the stock is down 72.6% since the results and currently trades at $12.18.

AT&T reported revenues of $31.56 billion, up 2.3% year on year. This number missed analysts' expectations by 0.6%. Zooming out, it was actually a satisfactory quarter as it recorded a beat of analysts' EPS estimates.
The stock is up 9.3% since reporting and currently trades at $24.34.

Optimum Communications reported revenues of $2.02 billion, down 5.8% year on year. This result lagged analysts' expectations by 0.5%. It was a slower quarter as it also recorded a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and EBITDA in line with analysts' estimates.
The stock is up 17.3% since reporting and currently trades at $0.92.

Over the past year, investors have been forced to repeatedly answer the same question: what is the market's biggest risk? The answer has changed several times, and each shift has reshaped market leadership.
Late in 2025 and early 2026, artificial intelligence became the market's primary uncertainty. Investors questioned whether AI would erode software pricing power and weaken competitive moats as AI made it easier to replicate once-differentiated products.
By the spring, technology took a back seat to geopolitics. The U.S. conflict with Iran briefly became the market's dominant narrative, raising concerns about oil prices, inflation, and global growth. But as energy markets remained orderly and fears of a prolonged supply disruption faded, investors quickly turned their focus back to fundamentals.

Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 4:10PM CDT
The latest update is out from Charter Communications ( (CHTR) ).
On September 15, 2026, Charter Communications announced that its board declared a regular quarterly cash dividend for holders of its Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. The dividend was set at $0.43750001 per share, payable in cash on October 15, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 30, 2026.
The preferred shares, originally issued in connection with Charter’s acquisition of Liberty Broadband Corporation, carry a 7% annual dividend rate, a $25 per-share liquidation preference plus accrued but unpaid dividends, and are mandatorily redeemable on March 9, 2039. The announcement underscores Charter’s ongoing capital-return commitments to preferred shareholders and clarifies the terms and schedule of distributions tied to the Liberty Broadband acquisition.

SpaceX’s Starlink Just Got More Powerful, and Cable Giants Comcast, Charter May Feel the Heat
SpaceX logo on smartphone with a rocket taking off in the background (Credit: Image via Shutterstock)
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:31 AM PDT 6 min read
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. could pose a growing threat to terrestrial broadband providers, particularly in rural and lower-density markets, MoffettNathanson analyst Craig Moffett said Tuesday as Starlink begins deploying higher-capacity V3 satellites.
Starlink Poses Bigger Threat to Comcast and Charter
The analyst sees SpaceX's Starlink becoming a more credible competitor to terrestrial broadband as Starship enables higher-capacity satellite deployments, although he expects fiber and cable networks to retain important speed advantages.
Moffett told CNBC that Starlink presents a much greater competitive challenge to terrestrial broadband providers such as Comcast Corp. and Charter Communications Inc. than to traditional wireless carriers such as AT&T Inc. and Verizon Communications Inc..

"The terrestrial broadband business where they deliver ISP service is a very credible product and will have a direct impact. It already is having a significant impact," Moffett said.
Investors are now trying to determine whether Starlink's impact will remain concentrated in rural and low-density markets or expand further into suburban and potentially some urban areas.
Moffett said the technology remains best suited to rural markets but can also serve some customers in denser areas.
V3 Satellites Strengthen Starlink's Offering
SpaceX's first Starship orbital flight marked an important milestone because the rocket deployed 26 V3 Starlink satellites, which Moffett said carry substantially more capacity and should improve the service.
However, he expects the transition to take time. Moffett said it will be after 2030 before most of the Starlink constellation consists of V3 satellites.
See Also: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time
Even with V3 satellites, he does not expect Starlink to match the speeds offered by terrestrial fiber or cable broadband.
That leaves pricing and customer segmentation as major competitive factors. Starlink could compete more effectively for value-oriented customers who prioritize lower costs over maximum broadband performance.
Moffett compared Starlink's challenge with the pressure Comcast and Charter already face from fixed wireless access.
The cable operators have responded by bundling broadband with wireless services, a strategy Moffett said has proven relatively successful.
The key question is how far Starlink can expand beyond its natural strength in rural markets and take customers from traditional broadband providers without matching the speed and quality of fiber and cable networks.

Building Wealth Across More Than Just the Market
Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry.
Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100. This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly.
For accredited investors looking beyond traditional stocks and bonds, Realberry provides access to institutional-quality real estate investments, including a preferred equity opportunity in the 297-room Hyatt Place Boston Seaport. The firm has invested across multiple property types and markets, with 13 million square feet of real estate across seven U.S. states and $481 million in cumulative distributions paid to investors as of Q4 2025.
Entertainment franchises can become valuable long-term assets when they successfully expand across multiple platforms. Skybound Entertainment, the company behind The Walking Dead and Invincible, develops original intellectual property that spans comics, television, film, video games, merchandise, and licensing. With more than 250 IPs in its portfolio and a strategy focused on retaining franchise rights while scaling successful stories across media, Skybound offers investors exposure to the growing entertainment and creator economy through a private company rather than traditional public market investments.
Coffee is a daily staple for millions of consumers, but investors rarely get direct exposure to the brands and supply chains behind it. Green Coffee Company offers a way to participate in the growth of the coffee market through its exclusive U.S. and Canadian distribution rights for Colombian brand Juan Valdez. With the brand expanding across major retailers including Target, Walgreens and Kroger, and GCC reporting 26X revenue growth over four years, the company is positioning itself to bring a well-known Colombian coffee brand to more consumers across North America.
As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth.
As electricity demand rises alongside AI, data centers, and renewable energy, long-duration energy storage is becoming increasingly important. Qnetic is developing a kinetic energy storage system designed to provide long-lasting, chemical-free electricity storage, offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting a more resilient and reliable power grid.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000, with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process.
Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches.
Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.

Spectrum's plan to activate AI capable computing across more than 1,000 embedded edge facilities gives Charter Communications (CHTR) a fresh angle on its broadband footprint, as investors reassess a sharply weaker year to date share performance.
Charter Communications has been rolling out these edge AI partnerships just as sentiment has weakened, with the share price down 27.96% over the past 30 days and 47.12% year to date, while the 1 year total shareholder return has fallen 59.77%. Charter Communications last closed at $110.67, while the leading narrative on the stock anchors on a fair value of $294.71, which paints a very different picture of what the business might be worth.

Charter Communications Sees Higher Broadband Losses, Better Financial Trends, UBS Says
Charter Communications' (CHTR) Q3 results should show steeper broadband subscriber losses even as financial metrics improve modestly, as rate actions in broadband and higher political ad spending help offset persistent competitive pressure from fiber and convergence, UBS Securities said in a note Monday.
The investment firm said its estimates exclude Cox, following the transaction's Aug. 20 closing, and will be updated once trending schedules are provided in mid-October. It attributed the expected pickup in broadband losses to fiber and convergence competition, with satellite also set to grow as Starlink expands its V3 constellation.
UBS said video should continue to outperform in the market, mobile net adds should slow year-over-year, and residential revenue trends should improve as July pricing actions take hold.
For 2027, UBS expects Cox to see accelerating declines while legacy Charter trends remain similar, with over $1 billion of cost synergies expected within three years of close.
UBS has a neutral rating on the stock with a price target of $140.

Charter Communications, Inc. stock (ISIN US16119P1084) closed at USD 145.77 on the Nasdaq on September 11, 2026, up 3.71 percent from the prior close, according to Nasdaq data cited by MarketBeat and Yahoo Finance. GuruFocus adds that at a share price of USD 145.77, Charter trades at a significant discount to a GF Value estimate of USD 371.96, indicating it may be around 60.8 percent undervalued based on that intrinsic value model.
Latest quarterly earnings underpin the debate
Charter Communications' most recent reported quarterly figures give investors a snapshot of the company's operating performance that underpins these diverging analyst views. According to MarketBeat, Charter last posted its quarterly earnings results on July 24, 2026.
For that quarter, Charter reported earnings per share (EPS) of USD 10.66, beating the analyst consensus estimate of USD 9.98 by USD 0.68 per share. The firm generated revenue of USD 13.53 billion in the quarter, slightly above analyst estimates of USD 13.51 billion, as detailed by MarketBeat.
The same report notes that Charter Communications delivered a net margin of 9.05 percent and a return on equity of 23.71 percent in this latest quarter, indicating continued profitability despite top-line pressure. However, quarterly revenue was down 1.7 percent compared to the same quarter a year earlier, when the company posted EPS of USD 9.18, underscoring the competitive and maturity challenges in its core cable and broadband markets, according to MarketBeat.
As a group, analysts tracked by MarketBeat expect Charter Communications to post EPS of 42.72 for the current fiscal year, indicating that the July 24, 2026 quarter forms part of a broader earnings trajectory that still implies solid profitability.
From a valuation perspective, Morgan Stanley's Equal Weight stance is framed by metrics that point to a relatively low multiple for the stock. According to Investing.com, Charter currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 3.76 and offers a free cash flow yield of roughly 18 percent, which the bank uses to justify its USD 150 price target despite competitive pressures.
GuruFocus similarly highlights a GF Score of 69 out of 100 for Charter Communications, describing a moderately strong overall fundamental profile with particular strengths in profitability and growth but weaker signals in financial strength and valuation.
At a current share price in the mid-USD 140s, this GF Value-based intrinsic value framework and the high free cash flow yield point to an apparent margin of safety that some investors may find attractive. Yet Wolfe Research's Underperform rating and USD 118 price target, reported by GuruFocus, reflect concerns about Charter's future performance in the face of intense competition, potential overbuilds by fiber and wireless providers, and questions about the combined entity's growth trajectory following strategic moves in the US cable and broadband landscape.

Consumer Discretionary - Wireless, Cable and Satellite Stocks Q2 In Review: Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) Vs Peers
The end of the earnings season is always a good time to take a step back and see who shined (and who didn't). Let's take a look at how consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks fared in Q2, starting with Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR).
The Consumer Discretionary sector, by definition, is made up of companies selling non-essential goods and services. When economic conditions deteriorate or tastes shift, consumers can easily cut back or eliminate these purchases. For long-term investors with five-year holding periods, this creates a structural challenge: the sector is inherently hit-driven, with low switching costs and fickle customers. As a result, only a handful of companies can reliably grow demand and compound earnings over long periods, which is why our bar is high and High Quality ratings are rare.Wireless, cable, and satellite companies provide pay-TV, broadband internet, and mobile connectivity through large fixed-infrastructure networks. Tailwinds include growing bandwidth consumption, bundling opportunities across video, internet, and wireless services, and rural broadband subsidies from government programs. However, headwinds are pronounced: cord-cutting continues to erode traditional video subscriber bases, capital expenditure requirements for network upgrades (such as fiber overbuilds and 5G rollouts) are substantial, and aggressive promotional pricing among competitors compresses margins. Regulatory oversight on pricing and net neutrality adds uncertainty, while streaming platforms increasingly bypass traditional distributors, reducing the value of the legacy pay-TV bundle.

CHARTER ANNOUNCES CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER TRANSITION
Stamford, CT. – Aug. 31, 2026 – Charter Communications (NASDAQ: CHTR) today announced that Jessica Fischer will
step down from her current position as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer on October 15, to relocate for another professional opportunity. The Company will begin a comprehensive search for her
replacement immediately.
Charter also named Kevin Howard, currently Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer & Controller, to the position of interim Chief Financial Officer
effective October 15. Mr. Howard will continue to work closely with Ms. Fischer to support ongoing financial operations and ensure a seamless leadership transition.
“I first met Jessica more than 15 years ago and actively recruited her to join our team at Charter,” said Chris Winfrey, President & CEO, Charter Communications.
“Since joining Charter nearly 10 years ago, and becoming our CFO in 2021, she has been a key part of our executive team. I am very proud of our work together and grateful for her many contributions in making Spectrum the leading broadband and video
“It has been a privilege to be part of Charter’s growth over the past decade,” said Ms. Fischer. “I have learned so much from Chris and this team and am grateful for the
opportunity and trust they placed in me to lead Charter’s financial operation.”
Mr. Howard brings over two decades of financial leadership to his role as Charter’s Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer & Controller, overseeing
accounting, tax, financial reporting, and ERP operations. He has led the financial integration of a number of Charter’s major transactions, including the acquisitions of Bresnan, Time Warner Cable, Bright House Networks and Cox Communications. He
previously served as Charter’s interim CFO in 2010.
Charter has not changed any of its previously provided financial outlook or financial policy.
Charter Communications, Inc. (NASDAQ: CHTR) is the leading broadband and video company in the nation and the fastest growing mobile provider in its
footprint, with services available to more than 70 million homes and small to large businesses across 45 states through its Spectrum brand. Founded in 1993, Charter has evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a
converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, the Company offers Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet®, Mobile, TV and Voice
products.
More information can be found at corporate.charter.com.
Media Contact:
Cameron Blanchard, cameron.blanchard@spectrum.com
Investor Relations:
Stefan Anninger, stefan.annigner@charter.com

The Consumer Discretionary sector, by definition, is made up of companies selling non-essential goods and services. When economic conditions deteriorate or tastes shift, consumers can easily cut back or eliminate these purchases. For long-term investors with five-year holding periods, this creates a structural challenge: the sector is inherently hit-driven, with low switching costs and fickle customers. As a result, only a handful of companies can reliably grow demand and compound earnings over long periods, which is why our bar is high and High Quality ratings are rare.Wireless, cable, and satellite companies provide pay-TV, broadband internet, and mobile connectivity through large fixed-infrastructure networks. Tailwinds include growing bandwidth consumption, bundling opportunities across video, internet, and wireless services, and rural broadband subsidies from government programs. However, headwinds are pronounced: cord-cutting continues to erode traditional video subscriber bases, capital expenditure requirements for network upgrades (such as fiber overbuilds and 5G rollouts) are substantial, and aggressive promotional pricing among competitors compresses margins. Regulatory oversight on pricing and net neutrality adds uncertainty, while streaming platforms increasingly bypass traditional distributors, reducing the value of the legacy pay-TV bundle. The 7 consumer discretionary - wireless, cable and satellite stocks we track reported a mixed Q2. As a group, revenues were in line with analysts' consensus estimates. Amidst this news, share prices of the companies have had a rough stretch. On average, they are down 12% since the latest earnings results. Operating as Spectrum, Charter (NASDAQ:CHTR) is a leading telecommunications company offering cable television, high-speed internet, and voice services across the United States. Charter reported revenues of $13.53 billion, down 1.7% year on year. This print was in line with analysts' expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with a beat of analysts' EPS estimates but a miss of analysts' EBITDA estimates.
